The season was started on 28 December 2020 and concluded with the [[2021 A-League Grand Final|Grand Final]] on 27 June 2021.{{cite web|url=https://www.a-league.com.au/news/start-date-confirmed-a-league-and-westfield-w-league|title=Start date confirmed for the A-League and Westfield W-League|work=A-League|date=15 October 2020}} The start of the season was later than previous seasons as a result of both the [[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]] and [[COVID-19 pandemic in New Zealand|New Zealand]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.smh.com.au/sport/soccer/a-league-set-for-winter-switch-after-securing-new-fox-sports-deal-20200619-p554dx.html|title=A-League set for winter switch after securing new Fox Sports deal|work=The Sydney Morning Herald|date=19 June 2020|access-date=8 September 2020}} [[Wellington Phoenix FC|Wellington Phoenix]] played the majority of their home matches at [[Wollongong Showground]] in [[Wollongong]] due to international travel restrictions.{{cite news|url=https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/sport/2020/11/football-wellington-phoenix-based-in-wollongong-for-a-league-season.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210116160431/https://www.newshub.co.nz/home/sport/2020/11/football-wellington-phoenix-based-in-wollongong-for-a-league-season.html|url-status=dead|archive-date=16 January 2021|title=Football: Wellington Phoenix based in Wollongong for A-League season|first=William|last=Hewett|newspaper=[[Newshub]]|date=24 November 2020}} [[Sydney FC]] were the defending champions and premiers, having won their record fifth and fourth titles respectively the [[2019–20 A-League|previous season]].
